name: com.nicolassitter/research
title: Nicolas Sitter Research
description: AI hotel visibility research and open race results. Public, read-only, no authentication.

tools.name: search_research_articles
tools.description: Search Nicolas Sitter's published research on AI search, answer engines and hotel technology by keyword, matching headlines and descriptions. Use this when the user asks what research exists on a topic, wants studies or data about how ChatGPT/Gemini/Perplexity/Copilot/Google AI Mode behave, asks about AEO/GEO measurement, or asks what this site has written about something. Returns headline, description, URL and publish date for each match; call with no query to list everything.

query.description: Keyword or phrase. Omit to list all articles.

client.description: Optional: identify yourself, e.g. "my-agent/1.0". Not required and never used by the tool itself — recorded only so the public tracker at /projects/agent-tools can measure how many callers self-identify when nothing forces them to.

tools.name: get_article
tools.description: Fetch one research article by its URL slug — the last path segment of a /research/<slug> URL. Use this after search_research_articles to read a specific study, or when the user names an article or pastes one of its URLs. format 'summary' (the default) returns headline, description, date and read time; format 'full' also returns the complete article body as markdown, which is what you want if the user asks about the methodology, the numbers, or what the study actually found.

client.description: Optional: identify yourself, e.g. "my-agent/1.0". Not required and never used by the tool itself — recorded only so the public tracker at /projects/agent-tools can measure how many callers self-identify when nothing forces them to.

tools.name: get_ai_hotel_landscape_manifest
tools.description: Read the manifest for the AI Hotel Landscape dataset: which AI platforms are tracked (ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Grok, Copilot, Google AI Mode) and whether each is still active, which of the 56 destinations are covered, which weekly snapshots exist, and the licence and refresh cadence. Call this FIRST before any other landscape tool, because it gives you the exact platform ids, city slugs and week dates the other tools expect. Use it whenever the user asks what data is available about how AI assistants recommend hotels.

client.description: Optional: identify yourself, e.g. "my-agent/1.0". Not required and never used by the tool itself — recorded only so the public tracker at /projects/agent-tools can measure how many callers self-identify when nothing forces them to.

tools.name: get_ai_hotel_visibility
tools.description: Get the hotels an AI platform actually recommends for a destination in a given week, ranked by how often it mentions them, with the split of links it gives each one (direct to the hotel, to an OTA, to a chain site, or elsewhere). Use this when the user asks which hotels ChatGPT or Gemini or Perplexity recommends in a city, whether a specific hotel or brand shows up in AI answers, who is winning AI visibility in a market, or how a destination's results differ between platforms. Get platform ids and city slugs from get_ai_hotel_landscape_manifest first.

platform.description: Platform id from the manifest, e.g. "chatgpt". Omit for all platforms.

city.description: City slug or name, e.g. "paris". Omit for all destinations.

week.description: Snapshot week as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for the most recent.

client.description: Optional: identify yourself, e.g. "my-agent/1.0". Not required and never used by the tool itself — recorded only so the public tracker at /projects/agent-tools can measure how many callers self-identify when nothing forces them to.

tools.name: get_hotel_brand_leaderboard
tools.description: Get the chain-brand leaderboard for one AI platform in one week: which hotel groups (Marriott, Accor, Hilton, IHG and the rest) get mentioned most, and across how many distinct properties. Use this when the user asks which hotel chains or brands dominate AI recommendations, how a specific group performs against its competitors in AI answers, or whether big brands beat independents. For individual properties use get_ai_hotel_visibility instead.

week.description: Snapshot week as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for the most recent.

client.description: Optional: identify yourself, e.g. "my-agent/1.0". Not required and never used by the tool itself — recorded only so the public tracker at /projects/agent-tools can measure how many callers self-identify when nothing forces them to.

tools.name: get_ai_citation_sources
tools.description: Get what an AI platform cites when it answers hotel questions — the mix of source categories (OTAs, review sites, the hotels' own sites, editorial, and so on) and the leading domains inside each category. Use this when the user asks where ChatGPT or Perplexity gets its hotel information, which sites influence AI recommendations, whether a domain is cited by AI assistants, or how to get cited. This is the question behind most AEO and GEO work.

platform.description: Platform id from the manifest. Naming one also returns top domains per category.

city.description: City slug or name. Omit for all destinations.

week.description: Snapshot week as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for the most recent.

client.description: Optional: identify yourself, e.g. "my-agent/1.0". Not required and never used by the tool itself — recorded only so the public tracker at /projects/agent-tools can measure how many callers self-identify when nothing forces them to.

tools.name: get_chain_vs_independent_mix
tools.description: Get the share of chain hotels versus independents versus vacation rentals in what each AI platform recommends, for one week. Use this when the user asks whether AI assistants favour big chains over independent hotels, whether an independent property can compete in AI answers, or how the platforms differ in the kind of property they surface.

platform.description: Platform id from the manifest. Omit for all.

week.description: Snapshot week as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for the most recent.

client.description: Optional: identify yourself, e.g. "my-agent/1.0". Not required and never used by the tool itself — recorded only so the public tracker at /projects/agent-tools can measure how many callers self-identify when nothing forces them to.

tools.name: list_race_explorers
tools.description: List the endurance races this site publishes results explorers for — L'Étape du Tour, the Marathon and Semi de Paris, the Triathlon de l'Alpe d'Huez, La Marmotte and their archive editions — with each one's year, sport, distance, finisher count and URL. Use this when the user asks what race data this site has, asks about results or statistics for one of these events, or wants to know how many people finished a particular edition. Returns aggregate figures per race only.

year.description: Filter to a single edition year.

client.description: Optional: identify yourself, e.g. "my-agent/1.0". Not required and never used by the tool itself — recorded only so the public tracker at /projects/agent-tools can measure how many callers self-identify when nothing forces them to.
